workload: Mixed CRLF, CR and LF whitespace inside identity-serialized JSON, with SSE framing performed by each package.

originalAttempt.note: The six-project run aborted on its first Better SSE trial; no successful throughput report was produced. Preceding partial log scores are not a completed comparison.

capture.note: Tiny correctness reproductions using the unmodified package-backed benchmark server; Better SSE/sveltekit-sse captures have one event, Fastify has two events (see its captureOptions). Captured bytes are replayed unchanged to native Node EventSource. These are not throughput samples.

findings: Better SSE with the benchmark identity serializer writes multiline JSON into one data field; JSON lines after the first are not data fields and native EventSource receives only an opening brace.
sveltekit-sse splits LF but leaves standalone CR inside a data field; native EventSource treats CR as a line ending and loses the payload line.

Fastify with @fastify/sse and the benchmark identity serializer also splits only LF, leaving standalone CR in serialized JSON. Native EventSource drops the payload line from both captured events. This is a failure of this mixed-newline/raw-JSON configuration, not a claim that ordinary compact JSON events are unsupported.
The former LF-only scorer falsely accepted sveltekit-sse and Fastify. The corrected independent scorer handles CR, LF and CRLF across byte boundaries and rejects all three captured package streams.

Earlier native/MinkSSE-only portable controls used fully LF-normalized output from both producers; their logical delivery validation is unaffected. The frozen old scorer preserves the recorded hash for audit.
Report all three package/workload results as validation failure / N/A, not zero throughput. Keep successful ASCII, Unicode and large-payload comparisons separate.
